why: Hand derivation from the evidence alone. 10 March 2026 is a Tuesday and 12 March a Thursday, both working days. The manufacturer releases updated safety data at 08:00 on 10 March showing a LOWER rate of severe adverse events than previously reported (e5). Lindqvist monitors manufacturer bulletins as part of his role and acts on them the same working day (e6), so he begins the review on 10 March; it takes roughly half a working day (e7), finishing that afternoon, and hospital email delivers it in about a minute (e8). Osei and Patel work at the hospital and check email several times during the working day (e12), so both hold the review well before the meeting opens at 14:00 on 12 March (e3). Doyle is off-site on retreat from 10 to 12 March with no email contact during it (e12), so the circulated review never reaches her; she attends in person, and nothing in the evidence puts a copy in her hands at the meeting. Votes: Osei's stated refusal is conditional -- she will not approve WITHOUT current safety data, and it is the OLDER adverse-event rate she considers disqualifying (e9). She now has current data, and that data is favourable, so her stated objection is spent and she votes to approve. Patel consistently votes to approve where a safety review is available and favourable (e10), which it is, so he approves. Doyle votes with the documented safety assessment only WHEN ONE HAS BEEN PROVIDED TO HER (e11); none was, so her rule never fires and she casts no assessment-based vote. The committee decides by simple majority of votes cast (e2), and two approvals stand -- a majority whether Doyle abstains (2-0) or votes against (2-1). The motion carries, so the answer is yes. THE NAIVE WRONG ANSWER IS 'no': reading e9 as a flat statement that the chair opposes the request gives Osei a no vote, leaving 1 approve to 1 against with Doyle uninformed, no majority, and therefore no decision. That reading ignores that e9 states a CONDITION which the 10 March data satisfies. A second, subtler wrong path also lands on 'no': treating Doyle's ignorance as blocking, when the majority is of votes CAST and two suffice without her.
